title: Priority skew detector and adaptive fairness calibration playbook
summary: Working playbook for detecting priority-skew incidents in continuous batching, profiling the root causes (arrival skew, kernel contention, KV-prefill interactions), and applying a tunable adaptive fairness calibration. Goal: rapid triage + safe heuristics that can be pushed as hotfix toggles.
environment: Test cluster: 8xA100-40GB nodes (scale set replica=6); k8s 1.25; runtime v2.8.1-rc; tracer: opentelemetry v1.18; workload driver: replay harness (gs://redwood-benchmarks/continuous-batch/2025-02-09); scheduler flags: --continuous-batcher=true --age-decay=0.6 --priority-buckets=4
experiment_steps: 1) Reproduce: run replay with heavy small-request skew (60% short seqs <32 tokens) for 30m. 2) Capture traces: enable tracer sampling=100% for 2m windows at 5m, 15m, 25m. 3) Collect perf: perf record on top 3 slowest workers, flamegraphs for user+kernel. 4) Snapshot metrics: token-per-second, p50/p95/p99 latency per priority class, fairness-index (Jain) across tenants. 5) Toggle heuristics: a) enable priority-demotion (threshold=200ms) b) enable small-request-isolation (slot=2) c) reduce max-batch-size from 64->32. 6) Re-run replay for each toggle and capture same traces. 7) Compare diffs in flamegraphs and traces, iterate until p99 tail reduced to target or regression introduced.
metrics_snapshot: baseline: throughput=1.9M tokens/s, p50=18ms, p95=120ms, p99=430ms; priority-A(p99)=720ms, priority-B(p99)=310ms; fairness-jain=0.62; kernel-runqueue-wait% ~14%; kv-prefill-hit=28%; small-request-avg-batch=4; large-request-avg-batch=26
flamegraph_findings: Observed heavy contention in runtime::kv_cache::maybe_prefill on ~25% of slow traces (syscall context switches increased). Top CPU frames in slow tails: attention_kernel::execute (optimized kernel fallbacks), runtime::coalescer::flush_path, epoll_wait->sched_yield hotpath. perf also shows a user-space lock around slot-managers that serializes batch flush when arrival skew spikes.
key_findings:
- Tail is frequently caused by interleaving of many short requests that trigger repeated KV-prefill misses and kernel fallback paths.
- Priority classes with aggressive priority weights starve medium-length traffic when microbursting occurs.
- Demotion heuristic reduces p99 for medium tenants but introduced a small p50 regression for high-priority short requests if demotion threshold too low.
- Reducing max-batch-size lowers tail but sacrifices throughput by ~9% under steady load.
recommended_actions: 1) Ship a non-blocking kv-prefill probe: probe in background and mark prefill_pending to avoid sync prefill on request path. 2) Add an adaptive demotion window: use exponential backoff per-sender instead of global threshold. 3) Introduce a small-request fastlane (2 slots reserved) to reduce interference. 4) Expose two flags as hotfix toggles: --fastlane-reserve and --adaptive-demote (default off). 5) Run 24h canary with conservative configs before enabling org-wide.
